messages:
ashley_support: @channel :rotating_light: High-priority customer escalation — multiple customers reporting 5xx/timeouts from Hosted API (generation endpoints). Started ~13:42 UTC, affecting endpoints behind prefix cache. We have a ticket from AcmeCorp with a repro.

ashley_support: Symptoms: lots of 502/504 gateway errors, timeouts from proxy -> runtime, and spikes in latency (p50 -> 1200ms, p95 -> 6s). Error payload shows downstream cache failures.

devex_ryan: Repro steps from AcmeCorp: curl against /v1/streams with header X-Model: x-small ; see repeated failures. They collected logs (pasted below).

devex_ryan: Logs snippet:
```
2026-03-14T13:42:01Z runtime: warn prefix-cache: redis GET prefix:abc123 -> ERR Connection refused
2026-03-14T13:42:01Z runtime: error request_id=req_9a8f response=502 upstream=prefix-cache
2026-03-14T13:42:02Z runtime: warn prefix-cache: redis TIMEOUT 5000ms cmd=GET
2026-03-14T13:42:03Z runtime: error request_id=req_9a90 gateway_timeout
```

mike_oncall: oncall here — acknowledged. Pulling metrics now. Any suggestion for immediate mitigations? Can we flip cache off per-route or route traffic to fallback model?

jordan_sre: I see a correlated alert from redis-cluster-prod: client_connections peaked and slowlog entries increased. Multiple nodes reporting 'maxclients reached' and 'connection reset by peer'. Likely a connection storm and eviction thrash.

redis-bot: ALERT: redis-cluster-prod primary-3 CPU high (92%), blocked clients > 1200, maxclients=1000. Recent events: node-restart at 13:41:56 UTC.

karen_reliability: Suggest immediate mitigations:
- Disable prefix/KV caching for affected host group (route-level config) so requests bypass Redis (set cache_policy=none)
- Increase runtime cache timeouts to 10s temporarily
- Fail traffic to model-variant: v2-no-kv (pre-built without external prefix caching) for the most sensitive routes
- Add circuit-breaker for redis errors at proxy layer (if not already) to return 503 faster

ashley_support: I've applied a temporary routing override for AcmeCorp to point to v2-no-kv and raised runtime cache timeout. Monitoring now.

devex_ryan: After reroute, AcmeCorp reports error rate dropped from 18% -> 2% and latency improved. They still see occasional 503s but not the flood of 502s.

jordan_sre: Infra action items: investigate why Redis hit maxclients, check client pooling, connection leakage in runtime, and why autoscaling didn't replace restarted node. Also roll forward a hotfix to pre-establish connection pools on startup.

mike_oncall: Created incident INC-2026-1234 https://tracker/redwood/INC-2026-1234. Assigning eng-infra and eng-runtime. Oncall pinged @jordan_sre and @karen_reliability.

ashley_support: Customer-facing update sent: 'We've mitigated the immediate impact by routing your traffic to a fallback variant and are doing a full investigation. We'll follow up with a timeline.' :thumbsup: 

karen_reliability: Postmortem owners: eng-infra (root cause and Redis ops), eng-runtime (connection pooling + graceful fallback), devex (customer repro + communication). ETA for preliminary RCA: 24 hours.

devex_ryan: Captured repro commands and logs in the incident ticket. Also attaching a minimal curl used by AcmeCorp:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Model: x-small" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":16}'
```

jordan_sre: Next steps: collect redis slowlog, check client_rejected metrics, confirm whether connection pooling bug was introduced in last runtime deploy (tag: runtime@2026.03.12). Rolling review now.

ashley_support: Closing loop — for now the customer is ok with reroute but wants SLA credit if root cause is infra. Keeping thread open until RCA.

mike_oncall: Thanks everyone. If we need a rollback plan for runtime, comment here. Otherwise standby for RCA updates.

redis-bot: NOTICE: redis-cluster-prod node primary-3 recovered (rejoined cluster) at 13:55:12 UTC.

ashley_support: Marking incident as mitigated in ticket. Final status: mitigation via route override + increased timeouts. Follow-up: full postmortem and customer SLA discussion.
